notes: Invariant held: no golden regenerated, every decide output identical (2,254/2,254) for each step and for the final tree.

(a) forward reuse: within one decide (and per world thread) the trunk (tokens + body) is cached by the exact bit pattern of the encoding fields it reads (scalars, card_idx, tok; rel_om/rel_oo only for nets that read R) plus net/table pointers; a hit is confirmed by full key equality, never by hash alone. 84% of trunk evaluations in a 1x1280 game were repeats (battle-box branches re-resolved along the chosen line, quiescence priors, leaf values). Cache is 2 generations x 4096 entries (~15 KB each) per thread; outside a decide nothing is cached.

(a) policy head: per-candidate logits are memoized on the shared trunk, keyed by the candidate row bits (si, ti, feats, budget) and net pointer; R(si,ti) is covered because rel_om is part of the trunk key whenever the net reads it.

Tried and dropped: a GameState-keyed cache (encode + trunk + priors). Only 35% of evaluations repeat the exact GameState (vs 84% repeating the encoding) and full-state compare/clone made decide 14% slower. Not committed.

(c) legal generation: adapter::legal_actions and apply::drain_own_interactions build the pending request and default dialog payload once (get_pending_request only mutates via an idempotent battle-phase normalization, nothing in between writes); selection_entries walks zones by reference with hash sets instead of cloning zones/uuids and quadratic string compares; uuid_index/slot_index/ProfileCache/LeaderCache/Vocab use a local Fx hasher (no new crate; lookups only, iteration order never read except dump_index_json whose map order was already random).

encode (outside the WP's named items, allowed by 'other large items'): the on-play probe ran a full GameState clone per probe (with_temp_dons, ~4.6% of instructions); it now runs on the live session inside Session::isolated with a new journaled Undo::DonPush for the temporary DONs, which is the same view as a fresh Session on a copy. The relation zero-fill (1,760 floats per encode) is skipped for nets with ablate=rel (R is never read then); Profile copies are made only when R is built.

Passive recalc: keywords are not cloned when already equal (the setter was a no-op then); is_reactive_passive no longer builds format!("{raw} {text}") (no pattern contains a space, so searching both parts separately is equivalent) and rejects early when '時、' is absent.

Not touched (WP rs-speed-b owns them): Move JSON representation, move_sig, py_game boundary, serde_json map hashing (SipHash inside serde_json IndexMap is still ~4% of instructions), encoding internals beyond the probe/zero-fill/profile-copy items above. Files touched are listed in outputs.changed_files for the later merge with rs-speed-b; the most likely overlaps are search/quiesce.rs (priors_keep / encode_for), net/nrel.rs (trunk/priors_from) and encode/*.

Remaining profile (after): apply 33%, legal 17%, encode 22% (on-play probe 8%, rel features 7%), forward 15%. Allocation (malloc/free) was ~23% of instructions before and is still the largest single cost; most of what is left is JSON move/pending construction (rs-speed-b) and the effect resolver's AST clones.

Measurement caveat: before/after latency runs were made side by side on two pinned cores (cores 0 and 1) rather than one after the other on core 0, to keep machine drift equal for both; the OPCG_PROF runs ran at the same time on cores 2/3. A separate 2-game check (cores 0/1, quiet) gave 79.3 s -> 50.1 s.
Target 1.5-2x: 1.50x on 1x1280 and 1.45x on 4x1280 for this WP alone (a + c); rs-speed-b (b + d) is expected to stack on top.
Environment: the container had no pytest/fastapi; installed opcg_sim/requirements.txt + pytest + pytest-xdist + httpx to run make test. maturin installed via pip. No code depends on that.
New prof counter n_trunk_hit (OPCG_PROF only). No tests added (per WP); the equality check scripts are work files and were not committed.
